newsitem.title: FINLAND: Edgy Helsinki ends down, off lows on Wall St rise.
newsitem.headline: Edgy Helsinki ends down, off lows on Wall St rise.

text.p: Shares ended an edgy session down but off earlier lows on Thursday as Wall St turned brighter -- but brokers were mixed on whether the recent retrenchment was enough to pave the way higher.
The FOX derivatives and portfolio benchmark closed 0.85 percent down at 1,229 and the HEX general index shed 0.69 percent to 3,576. Volume was a scant 546 million markka.

One broker said the market found clear encouragement in signs that U.S. growth is producing few inflationary pressures, but another said the market was not on yet firm ground, and nervousness remained.
UPM led forestries down as sellers locked in when its H1 report, although at the top end of market forecasts, failed to deliver a major positive surprise, brokers said.

"UPM and Enso results were not quite diamonds," said one broker of the recent rash of first-half reports. However, Metsa-Serla picked up 1.00 markka or about three percent to close at 52.50 in relatively lively trade.

Analysts clearly remain split on prospects for forestry shares: some turned more bullish recently, encouraged by the companies' more optimistic comments. But doubters remain, predicting a volatile spell for the rest of the year.
